problem: Which of the following is equivalent to $\frac{1}{{tan}^{2}⁡x{sec}^{2}⁡x-{tan}^{4}⁡x+1}?$

feedback.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to ${tan}^{2}⁡x{sec}^{2}⁡x-{tan}^{2}⁡x-1?$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we recall the different forms of the secant-tangent Identity:

$$
\begin{aligned} & (1) & 1+{tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x \\  & (2) & {tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x-1 \\  & (3) & {sec}^{2}⁡x-{tan}^{2}⁡x=1\end{aligned}
$$

We can simplify our expression using $(2),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{tan}^{2}⁡x{sec}^{2}⁡x-{tan}^{2}⁡x-1 & ={tan}^{2}⁡x({sec}^{2}⁡x-1)-1 \\  & ={tan}^{2}⁡x({tan}^{2}⁡x)-1 \\  & ={tan}^{4}⁡x-1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
{tan}^{2}⁡x{sec}^{2}⁡x-{tan}^{2}⁡x-1={tan}^{4}⁡x-1.
$$
